tools.name: find_poems
tools.description: Search the library. For a situation or a wish ("I just lost my dad", "a poem to thank my mother", "something calm for a ten-year-old", "an easy first poem to learn by heart"), set what the reader needs first: need, or occasion and recipient for a poem to send, audience, easy_to_memorise, easy_to_rea

tools.name: get_poem
tools.description: One poem by its id (from find_poems or a poem page URL): title, poet, language, the number of lines and stanzas, the opening of the text (a poem of 1 to 3 lines whole), a short summary when the library has one, and the links to the full poem, its analysis (when there is one) and the trainer to learn

tools.name: poem_of_the_day
tools.description: Today's poem of the day in a language (English by default): title, poet, opening lines (a poem of 1 to 3 lines whole) and link.

tools.name: about_poet
tools.description: A poet in the library by name or by slug (the last part of the poet page URL): the biography (up to about 1,500 characters) and a one-line summary of it, the number of poems, up to 10 poems with links, and the poet page.

tools.name: library_guide
tools.description: What the library offers in one language, to turn a request into filters: the 8 moods (names in that language), the most used tags of that language (most used first) and its collections (title and slug). Call it to narrow find_poems (need, occasion, audience) with one mood and 1–3 tags, or to pick a

tools.name: list_collections
tools.description: For an occasion or a feeling (a wedding, a funeral, missing someone, autumn), the library's collections of poems in a language (all languages when none is given): title, slug, a short introduction and the link. Pick the closest and call get_collection with its slug. Collections exist in English, Rus

tools.name: get_collection
tools.description: One collection by its slug (from library_guide or list_collections): title, introduction, link and up to 8 of its poems with the poet, the number of lines, the opening lines (a poem of 1 to 3 lines whole), one sentence on what the poem feels like (use it to choose, it is not the poet's words) and th

tools.name: get_analysis
tools.description: The summary of a poem and the opening of its analysis (about 1,200 characters at most), with links to the summary and analysis pages, when the library has them. Written in the language of the poem.

tools.name: learn_by_heart
tools.description: A plan to learn a poem by heart in a number of days (7 by default, 3 to 14): its stanzas and lines, which stanzas to learn on which day with a time estimate, the review days after, and the link to the free web trainer that does the drilling. No poem in mind: find_poems with easy_to_memorise suggests

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_poem · Public sink: find_poems.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_poem · Public sink: find_poems

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
